title: Hackers Use GitHub-Hosted Poem to Control PoeLLM Malware Targeting AI Infrastructure
key_facts: A poem titled 'On the Nature of Connection' hosted in a GitHub repository guides the PoeLLM malware to its command-and-control servers.

PoeLLM extracts four words or phrases from the poem, maps each to a number with an internal dictionary, and the four numbers form the IPv4 address of the current control server; changing the words redirects infected machines.
Active since at least April 2026; researchers observed 11 poem updates after the first commit on 13 April.
It targets internet-facing LiteLLM, Ollama, Gotenberg and Gitea servers and installs XMRig and Iron cryptocurrency miners; infected servers also scan and exploit others.

Lumen's Black Lotus Labs published its report on 7 Oct 2026; the overview gives more than 3,400 affected servers while some sections keep an earlier figure of almost 2,200; most victims are in the US and Western Europe.
One likely LiteLLM attack path is command injection flaw CVE-2026-42271.
Italian-language code comments suggest an Italian-speaking operator, not a confirmed identity.
quote_evidence: Hackers are using a poem hosted on GitHub to guide PoeLLM malware toward its command-and-control servers, turning exposed AI infrastructure into a growing cryptocurrency-mining botnet.
Changing those words lets the attacker redirect infected machines without replacing the malware.
Italian-language code comments and network evidence suggest an Italian-speaking operator, not a confirmed identity.
why_it_matters_hint: Exposed AI servers are being hijacked for crypto mining using a hard-to-block poem trick, so AI tools need the same patching and exposure checks as other servers.
event_date: Active since April 2026; Lumen report 7 Oct 2026
notes: Secondary report of Lumen's Black Lotus Labs research (original not opened). The article's victim counts are inconsistent (3,400 versus almost 2,200).
